findings.description: deliver is now async, but flush calls it without await. The call returns a coroutine object, which is always truthy, so every digest is treated as delivered. Nothing is ever sent, because the coroutine never runs (Python also emits a 'never awaited' warning). Pending lines are deleted, so digests are silently lost and `failed` is always empty.
findings.title: deliver() coroutine is not awaited in flush()

findings.description: flush now awaits during delivery, so add() can run in the meantime. The `sent` snapshot handles appends, but `self._pending[recipient]` is held as a local list. If another flush runs concurrently, or the key is deleted and re-created, the lines are removed twice or from a stale list. Concurrent flushes can also double-send digests. `sorted(self._pending)` is a snapshot, but `self._pending[recipient]` on a key deleted by another flush would create a new empty list and send an empty digest.
findings.suggestion: Guard flush with an asyncio.Lock, or snapshot the lines with `lines = list(self._pending[recipient])` and remove only the sent prefix afterwards, using `.get` to handle missing keys.
findings.title: Queue mutation across await can drop or corrupt lines
